The text presents the lighthouse keeper as a figure of profound isolation, yet his role is fundamentally connective. The lighthouse itself serves as a potent symbol: it stands apart from the world, yet its light is essential for others to navigate safely. This duality suggests an implicit theme of the paradox of solitude—that one can be physically or emotionally isolated while still holding a vital, guiding purpose for others. The "darkness" represents the chaos or uncertainty of life, while the keeper’s vigilance symbolizes the human need for stability and direction. The visits of the seafarers highlight the intermittent but necessary nature of human connection; the keeper is not entirely alone, but his interactions are defined by his function as a guide rather than a peer. This implies that purpose can be found in service to others, even within a framework of separation.
